description: PyNite is a Python finite-element library for structural engineers. It analyses elastic three-dimensional frames and plates and includes modal, P-delta and steel-frame pushover analysis. Users construct nodes, members, supports, loads and load combinations in Python; the solver returns reactions, displacements, member forces and diagrams. A model can represent a building frame, bridge component or foundation at the scale chosen by the modeller. The README provides a pip command, examples and documentation, and GitHub metadata identifies the MIT licence. The maintainers say accuracy remains a priority but give no guarantee that results are error free. Pushover is limited to supported steel sections, and mat-foundation features have had experimental status. PyNite can provide a structural-response component in infrastructure hazard studies, provided users independently check element assumptions and boundary conditions. The related catalogue OpenSees record is a separate structural solver, not a copy of PyNite. No solver or model input was downloaded or executed.
inputs: Structural geometry, element properties, supports and load cases
